title: Ingress variant weight probe — notebook
content:
Context:
This is a personal notebook sketching a lightweight probe mechanism to exercise and measure per-variant ingress weight effects without full rollout plumbing. Goal is to have a small runtime-safe harness that can: (1) inject traffic according to a candidate weight distribution, (2) collect latency/cost/response-quality signals, (3) surface divergence vs baseline, and (4) produce a minimal report to drive rollouts.

Why: We frequently tweak routing weights (model variants, quant profiles, regions, tiers) but lack an automated micro-experiment that can validate the operational impact before an actual weighted rollout. Current canary tooling is heavy and requires route changes + long-lived traffic shaping. Probe should be cheap, ephemeral, low-risk.

Requirements (high-level):
- Non-invasive: should not require global routing changes, only a probe client and a probe executor that can hit existing ingress endpoints.
- Replayable: deterministic seed for request selection for repeat runs.
- Representative: sample mix should approximate real production distribution (by route, prompt length bucket, user tier).
- Lightweight metrics: per-token latency p50/p95, model time, cost-est (tokens * unit-cost), error/timeout rate, quality delta vs baseline (BLEU / embedding-sim / eval prompt set).
- Safe: rate-limited, tenant-aware, respects opt-out, uses test tokens/tenants where possible.

Probe components (rough):
1) Controller (k8s job or ephemeral lambda) - orchestrates a run, reads config, collates results.
2) Probe client library - uniform way to send requests to Redwood API variants with pluggable sampling strategies.
3) Sample engine - picks requests from an anonymized production sample store (or synthetic generator).
4) Metrics sink - pushes to internal metrics (prom + trace) and writes a summary artifact (json) to S3/drive.
5) Comparator - simple script that computes effect sizes vs baseline run.

API shape (probe client snippets) - informal:
- POST /probe/run -> {name, target_route, variants: [{id, weight}], sample_strategy, duration_seconds, max_qps}
- GET /probe/run/{id}/status -> {state, started_at, finished_at, metrics_url}
- GET /probe/run/{id}/report -> {summary_url, raw_results_url}

Example local config (yaml-style):
---
name: small-weight-check
target_route: /v1/generate:chat
variants:
  - id: model-x-quant-8
    weight: 0.2
  - id: model-x-quant-4
    weight: 0.8
sample_strategy:
  type: production-bucket
  buckets: [short, medium, long]
  seed: 42342
duration_seconds: 900
max_qps: 10
output_bucket: s3://ci-probes/ingress-weights/
---

Sampling notes:
- If production sample store is unavailable, fallback to synthetic generation with length and intent tags.
- Prefer picking recent traffic (last 24h) or historical canonical workloads (support chat+completion+embed).

Signals and lightweight quality check:
- Latency: client-observed per-request latency and server-tokens-per-second stamping.
- Cost proxy: token_count * variant_unit_cost (from pricing table) aggregated per-run.
- Quality: embed similarity to baseline -> compute 1k-shot eval on canonical prompt set; produce mean/median.
- Anomalies: abnormal traceback, 5xx spikes, increased timeout fraction.

ASCII diagram (end-to-end):

[Controller] --start--> [Sample Engine] --provides--> [Probe Client X N] ==> [Ingress Load Balancer] -> [Serving Runtime (variants)]
                                                       
Probe clients stream results -> [Metrics Sink (prom)] + [Raw results -> S3] -> [Comparator] -> [Report JSON]

Operational safety and guardrails:
- Run only under a dedicated probe API key with tight ACLs.
- Default traffic cap per run (max_qps) and global budget per day.
- Auto-abort if 5xx > threshold or latency > threshold x baseline.
- Ensure probe keys are tied to internal tenant to avoid cross-tenant interference.

Run orchestration ideas (cheap modes):
- Local dev: single-node run using sample file, produce local report.
- CI mode: run after infra/config change PRs to validate routing delta.
- Nightly baseline check: scheduled nightly run against low-weight variant to detect regressions.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to ensure probe represents edge-case tail behavior? (need stratified sampling by intent + length + tenant)
- Should the probe mutate real routing metrics (billing flags)? probably not; use internal billing multiplier to simulate cost.
- Where to store/run comparator and how to version baseline runs? Need a compact run manifest with metadata (commit, model-version, kernel).
- Privacy: what parts of sample store are safe to use? anonymize prompt content; only keep intent hash.

Example minimal report (conceptual):
{
  run_id: "20241202-smw1",
  started_at: "2024-12-02T03:12:00Z",
  duration_seconds: "900",
  variant_summary: ["model-x-quant-8:20%","model-x-quant-4:80%"],
  metrics: ["p50_latency_ms: 52","p95_latency_ms: 210","cost_delta_pct: +12.4","quality_delta_embed_cos_sim: -0.003"],
  anomalies: ["5xx_spike: false","timeout_rate: 0.001"]
}

TODOs (short):
- [ ] prototype client lib (python) w/ sample-strategy hooks (Jordan)
- [ ] create minimal controller k8s job template (Priya)
- [ ] stash anonymized sample extractor + small seed set (Ethan)
- [ ] add auto-abort heuristic into controller
- [ ] wire report -> S3 + send slack notification channel (#ingress-probes)

Notes-to-self / heuristics:
- Keep runs short (5–15m) for rapid feedback; longer runs for low-signal variants.
- Use deterministic seeds for A/B comparability.
- Start with token-latency and cost-est; add quality checks after baseline is stable.

References / inspirations:
- existing canary tooling PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/421
- metric schema: metrics://ingress/latency (note: internal doc)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-1423 (ingress variant rollout audit)

If useful, will convert this into a short PoC repo with: client, controller helm job, comparator script, and a tiny dashboard. Quick sketch of repo layout in mind:
- probe-client/ (pip package)
- controller/ (k8s job manifest + controller runner)
- samples/ (seed files)
- comparator/ (scripts + report generator)

End of notebook.
summary: Sketch for a lightweight ingress variant-weight probing harness: components, API shapes, sampling strategy, metrics, ASCII diagram, TODOs, and open questions. Intended as a personal planning doc to turn into a PoC.
